description: Enumerate every plugin that could be loaded into this solet on the next restart. The verb walks the canonical 'ananta.plugins' entry-point group (the same group plugin_discovery uses at startup) and also scans the repo's plugins/ directory for source-tree candidates that are not yet installed. Each row carries the plugin name, a 'source' discriminator ('installed_entry_point' when the plugin is already registered as an entry point and can be referenced by name in the next manifest, vs. 'available_uninstalled' when the plugin sits on disk under plugins/<name>/ with a valid plugin.yaml or pyproject.toml but is not yet pip-installed and would need install_plugin_from_path first), a 'has_metadata' flag, an optional 'version' string, an optional 'description' string sourced from plugin.yaml or distribution Summary, and an 'implements' list of interface short names parsed from plugin.yaml's implements block. The list is sorted alphabetically by name. Use this verb to populate apply_manifest's diff preview, to confirm that a plugin you intend to add to the next manifest is in fact installable (or to learn that it must be installed first), and to take inventory before drafting a new profile manifest.
embedding_description: Enumerate every plugin loadable on next restart. Walks ananta.plugins entry-point group + scans plugins/ source tree. Each row: name, source (installed_entry_point vs available_uninstalled), has_metadata, version, description, implements list. Use before apply_manifest to inventory + confirm installability; install_plugin_from_path first if source=available_uninstalled. Read-only.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Mapping with one key 'plugins' whose value is a list of per-plugin records. Each record has: name (str), source ('installed_entry_point' or 'available_uninstalled'), has_metadata (bool), version (str or null), description (str or null), implements (list of interface short names from plugin.yaml).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: When the caller is preparing a new manifest, group the response by source: list 'installed_entry_point' rows first (these can be added to the manifest as-is) and 'available_uninstalled' rows second (these need install_plugin_from_path first). Surface 'description' compactly per row; 'implements' is informational for cross-checking service-binding intent. If the list is empty, say so explicitly — it indicates the solet image lacks plugins entirely and is almost certainly broken.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Treat the response as a snapshot for the next decision. If a needed plugin is in 'available_uninstalled', the natural next call is install_plugin_from_path. If it is in 'installed_entry_point', the next call is apply_manifest with the new manifest shape. Do NOT call list_available_plugins again immediately afterwards to verify; one read is authoritative for the current tick.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Read-only enumeration of plugins available to apply_manifest on the next restart, sourced from installed entry points plus repo-tree directories with plugin.yaml or pyproject.toml
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: ValueError (raised by malformed plugin.yaml or pyproject.toml under plugins/<name>/) — surfaces as a logged warning per file; the enumeration continues with the remaining rows. No side effects; the verb has no per-call mutable state and no orchestrator dependencies beyond the running Python interpreter.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: If a plugin you expected is missing, check that its entry point is registered in pyproject.toml ([project.entry-points."ananta.plugins"]) or that its directory ships plugin.yaml or pyproject.toml. If a plugin appears with version=null and description=null, look at the warning log for parse errors; the file is reachable but malformed.
